heroHeadline: PLA Second 'Joint Combat Readiness Patrol' in One Week — 26 Sorties May 26 (YY-20 Refueling Photographed; 100+ Ships Along First Island Chain); 10 Sorties May 27 (9 Cross Median N/C/SW ADIZ); NT$295B Arms Budget Clears Committee, Floor Vote Expected May 29 — 4 Days to HIMARS Deadline
heroSubtitle: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 26 PLA aircraft sorties on May 26, 2026 — the second explicitly designated 'joint combat readiness patrol' within one week following a similar operation approximately May 19 — with 7 PLAN vessels simultaneously operating around Taiwan. Taiwan's NSC Secretary-General Joseph Wu condemned the patrols as 'unprovoked' and disclosed that China had deployed more than 100 ships along the First Island Chain (Japan through Taiwan to the Philippines) in the days following the Trump-Xi summit. Taiwan's F-16s photographed a PLA YY-20 aerial refueling tanker conducting mid-air refueling of two fighters during the patrol. On May 27, Taiwan detected 10 PLA sorties with 9 of 10 crossing the median line into northern, central, and southwestern ADIZ sectors simultaneously — a 90% crossing rate indicating sustained multi-sector access penetration as a normalized pattern. The full May 2026 sortie sequence now stands: 4→29→1→2→1→0→22→12→8→12→7→9→2→3→15→6→7→13→24→7→6→16→4→9→26→10. On the legislative front, Taiwan's combined Foreign Affairs/National Defense and Finance Committees cleared the NT$295 billion special procurement budget on May 27 with only a nominal NT$2 million cut, paving the way for a floor vote expected as early as May 29 — just two days before the May 31 HIMARS first payment (NT$800 million) deadline. Defense Minister Wellington Koo testified on May 26 that HIMARS provides Taiwan with 300 km deep-strike capability against PLA missile launch platforms. The Executive Yuan has authorized reserve funds as a payment backstop. Diplomatically, Taiwan's Foreign Minister confirmed on May 25 that a Trump-Lai call would be 'positive' but that no planning talks have taken place.
